## TL;DR

Task #1058 removes recent-activity suffixes from running Board and Pipeline status lines and exposes the timing through the shared styled tooltip on mouse hover and keyboard focus. Review 9’s timestamp fallback now validates each candidate, preferring agent activity, then the running start, then the task’s state time. When that final source is the only valid one, Board hints label it as time in the state; Pipeline keeps its state elapsed visible. The shared tooltip implementation was restored from `main`, preserving its existing interactions. Touch pinning remains out of scope per the owner decision. The unrelated task bookkeeping changes reported in Review 9 were restored from `main`.

## Work and rationale

The recency formatter is shared by Board and Pipeline surfaces. Its timestamp selector uses `Number.isFinite(Date.parse(value))`, so malformed telemetry cannot mask a valid fallback. TaskCard keeps the last real activity or running start as the activity signal used for silence detection. For its explanatory popover, if neither source is usable, it formats `task.updated_at` as “In this state for …” with the timestamp. That distinction avoids describing a state-change timestamp as agent output. The check-progress display uses the same activity/state-time popover as the status hint.

PipelineView continues to pass a validated activity timestamp from the activity store or running start. PipelineCard checks the timestamp before hiding elapsed text. If it is missing or invalid, it leaves the elapsed state time visible in both the status and check-progress layouts. This retains a useful duration for idle review and close-out rows and for active rows without usable activity telemetry. If valid activity exists, its “Active … ago” copy appears on the status line’s shared tooltip instead.

The touch-related tooltip change was not needed for this feature. I restored `tooltip.ts` from `main` and removed the test that directly asserted touch pointer behavior. Board and Pipeline recency tests still exercise only hover and keyboard focus. The existing shared tooltip provides those entry points; no recency-specific pointer listeners or timers were introduced.

Review 9 also found that the branch carried task bookkeeping for unrelated tasks. I restored the 1060, 1061, 1067, 1068, 1069, 1070, and 1067 report paths from `main`, together with the main copy of task 1058. A merge-tree inspection showed bookkeeping conflicts between the task branch and current main; the restored main copies leave the working tree ready for RepoOS to checkpoint and validate. No `repoos.toml` changes were made.

## Approaches tried

The previous timestamp selection already skipped invalid values for the activity and running-start pair, but returned no value if both failed. I kept that pair separate for silence detection and added a state-time fallback only to visible timing copy. This prevents old `updated_at` values from being mistaken for recent agent activity while ensuring the user still sees timing. Pipeline already had a state elapsed value, so the fix there was to validate `lastActivityAt` with a finite parse and preserve elapsed whenever that activity tip is unavailable.

For the shared tooltip, I compared the working copy with the branch’s `main` version and restored the shared implementation rather than adding a task-specific touch exception. The focused regression suite passed across the card and pipeline test files. The final `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed: 366 selected test files, 5,101 tests passed, one skipped, followed by the UI smoke test and rendered contrast audit. The UI build also passed after the final UI edits.

After a remote handoff run reported failures in `debugger-integration.test.ts`, I ran that file alone in the feature worktree and against a clean archive of `main`. All seven tests passed in both contexts, so the reported failure did not reproduce locally or on main.

## Challenges and blockers

The branch’s existing WIP history includes unrelated task-file removals and edits relative to current main. Restoring those paths stages the main versions so RepoOS can include them in its next checkpoint. The merge-tree preview reported bookkeeping conflicts; the requested unrelated task paths were restored from main, as was task 1058’s task file. A direct merge stopped on those conflicts, and `repoos sync 1058` refused because the engineer turn is still active. I aborted the conflicted merge, restored the main copies, and left branch history for RepoOS’s managed integration. The final changed-path check passed on this tree. No `repoos.toml` changes were made.

## Key learnings

Activity time and state time answer different questions. A running timestamp should drive “Active … ago” and silence detection; a task state timestamp should drive “In this state for …” when activity data cannot be trusted. Keeping those sources distinct avoids false healthy or stuck signals while preventing blank timing. Also, a global tooltip change has repo-wide interaction consequences, so restoring its established behavior is simpler and safer than introducing feature-specific pointer handling.
